newsitem.title: USA: USDA issues final rules for new EQIP program.
newsitem.headline: USDA issues final rules for new EQIP program.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday laid out the final rules for its newEnvironmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP), releasing $200 million in funds for water quality and other conservation work.

The program provides cost-share money and expert advice to crop and livestock farmers who want to make environmental and conservation improvements. EQIP has an annual budget of $200 million through 2002. Half the money is slated for livestock farmers.

Since the program was created as part of the 1996 Farm Bill there has been a dispute over how large a livestock operation can qualify. Congress stipulated that big operations not be eligible for cost-share aid for animal waste management.

In its final rules, the department defined large livestock operations as those with more than 1,000 animal units. However, it gave states flexibility to modify the national standard to meet their conservation needs.

"Because of the differences in operations and environmental circumstances across the country, the definition of a large confined livestock operation may be determined in each state by the National Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) state conservationist, after consultation with the state technical committee and approved by the NCRS chief," USDA said.

USDA said the program will provide cost-share aid for up to 75 percent of the cost for conservation practices such as grassed waterways, filter strips, manure management and wildlife habitat enhancement. It will also offer incentive payments to producers who pursue certain land management.
All payments are limited to $10,000 per person per year and $50,000 for the length of a contract. Contracts can run from five to 10 years, USDA said.
